summary: Iteration 13 — media endpoint auth hardening. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_media_authz.py (28 tests, all green) covering: 401 without token, 401 for malformed bearer/query token, 404 for valid token + missing file, owner 200 via bearer AND ?token= query param, stranger student 404 (via both auth channels), assigned faculty 200, path-traversal guards, and Edit & Finish smoke (version create, faculty approve rough_cut, faculty final-approve blocked by rights/accessibility/delivery gate). Full backend regression: 220/220 passed. Found + fixed TWO one-line field-name typos in the ownership scoping logic that silently defeated the media authorization for /api/generated/ and /api/music-audio/ — details below.

critical.issue: Ownership check was querying db.assets on field `file_path` but the Asset model stores the URL on field `url`. Result: `linked_project_id` was ALWAYS None for AI-saved assets, so _media_project_check never fired and any authenticated user could fetch any other user's saved AI images by filename. Fixed in place: server.py:1199 now queries {"url": {"$regex": filename}}. Verified by test_generated_stranger_404 (now green).

Ownership check was querying db.music_tracks on field `audio_url` but the MusicTrack model stores the file URL on field `music_url`. Result: ownership check never fired for uploaded music files — any authenticated user could fetch any other user's uploaded music. Fixed in place: server.py:1316 now queries {"music_url": {"$regex": filename}}. Verified by test_music_audio_stranger_404 (now green).

action_items: Review the two field-name fixes applied to server.py (assets.url regex + music_tracks.music_url regex) — the security scoping now works, but the fact that these typos slipped through means there is NO integration test covering cross-user media reads in the existing suite until this iteration. Please keep test_media_authz.py in regression.

Filename policy on /api/generated/ and /api/music-audio/ uses `.replace('_','').replace('-','').replace('.','').isalnum()` which permits any UTF-8 alphanumeric (e.g. Cyrillic homoglyphs, RTL chars). Consider tightening to an explicit `re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9._-]+', filename)` for defense in depth. Not exploited today.

The /api/generated/ endpoint intentionally serves orphan (no db row) files to any authenticated user — documented behaviour in the request. Consider tracking owner_id on the generated file itself (e.g. rename to <owner_id>_<uuid>.png at write-time) if you want to close this last gap.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to 2284 lines — should be split (media endpoints, finish endpoints, ai endpoints each deserve their own module).
_authenticate_media uses ?token= query param for auth — necessary for /

Ownership scoping is defense-in-depth on top of the 401 gate but relies on Mongo regex against a filename — regex-injection-safe here because the filename is validated `.isalnum()`-style first, but if that guard is ever relaxed the regex becomes an injection vector. Consider re.escape() at minimum.

rca of the issue: RCA: The main agent introduced _media_project_check() to enforce ownership on the three media endpoints, but the two OLDER endpoints (/generated and /music-audio) look up the linked project by grepping filename against a Mongo field — and those field names were WRONG for the actual schema. `db.assets` uses `url` (not `file_path`) and `db.music_tracks` uses `music_url` (not `audio_url`). Because Mongo returns None for a non-matching query, `linked_project_id` stayed None and the ownership check silently skipped. Reproduction: seed a /generated (via POST /api/ai/image with save_as_asset=True + project_id) or a /music-audio (via POST /projects/{id}/music/upload) as student A, then register student B and GET the file URL with B's bearer token — before the fix returned 200 with the file body; after returned 404. Mitigation applied: fixed both field names to match the actual schema (assets.url, music_tracks.music_url). Long-term mitigation: add cross-user negative tests (this iteration's test_media_authz.py) to regression.
